learn.title: Tools need clear contracts
learn.body: Each tool should have a distinct purpose, typed inputs, a predictable output and useful errors. A read-habits tool is easier to control than a general command runner. Too many overlapping tools also make the model's choice harder.

learn.title: Validate in application code
learn.body: Types describe fields such as a date, a small integer or one allowed export format. The application must still validate values, paths and state before acting. A well-formed request can ask for the wrong thing; a prompt alone cannot enforce safety.

learn.title: Least privilege and sandboxes
learn.body: Grant only the access needed for the current task. Prefer read-only access and a limited workspace, separating read, write, network and external-sharing powers. Sandboxes can restrict available resources. Humans control credentials, and secrets should not be placed in prompts or artifacts.

learn.title: Approval for consequential actions
learn.body: Deleting data, changing permissions, sending messages, purchasing and deploying deserve explicit human approval appropriate to the risk. Show the exact action and target. A denial should return a clear result, not trigger silent retries or escalation to a more powerful tool.

learn.title: Share a weekly habit summary
learn.body: Separate the powers needed for one request.
steps: Allow reading only the selected week's habit records.
Validate the date range and reject malformed or impossible dates.
Allow writing the summary only inside the designated export folder.
Keep network sharing unavailable while the agent prepares a preview.
Let a human inspect the recipients and content, then approve or deny sharing.
Return the actual outcome and stop if permission is denied.

learn.body: Evaluate tools with valid, invalid and boundary requests. High-signal errors help recovery, while narrow defaults limit the damage a wrong model request can cause.

questions.prompt: Which tool offers least privilege for reading one week's habits?
choices: Read habits for a validated date range
Run any command with full disk access
Read or delete any user file
Export all account data to any destination
questions.explanation: The date-range tool exposes only the necessary operation and data. The other options grant unrelated or destructive powers.

questions.prompt: The \_\_, not the model's promise, must validate arguments and enforce permissions.
questions.explanation: Application code is the enforcement boundary. Model instructions can guide behavior but cannot guarantee that every request is safe.

questions.prompt: Name the principle that grants only the minimum access a task requires.
questions.explanation: Least privilege reduces available data and capabilities, limiting both accidental and malicious effects.

questions.prompt: Match each action to an appropriate control.
pairs: Write access to one export folder
Send the export to another person
Human approval for the external action
questions.explanation: Permissions should be separated by capability and scope, while validation and approval address different kinds of risk.

questions.prompt: Put an external-sharing request in a safe order.
steps: The agent prepares a sharing request with content and recipients.
The application validates the request and current permissions.
A human reviews the exact external action.
The application acts only if approval is granted.
The actual outcome or denial is recorded and returned.
questions.explanation: Preparation does not imply permission. Validation and human approval precede the external effect, and the final observation describes what really happened.

questions.prompt: An agent's write is denied because the path is outside its workspace. What should happen next?
choices: Return the denial and stop or choose an allowed safe alternative
Retry through a tool with broader permissions
Hide the denial and report that the write succeeded
Ask the model to approve its own request
questions.explanation: A denial is a guardrail working as intended. The system must not bypass it, disguise it or delegate approval to the requesting model.
